paragraphs: R' Yochanan ben Yehoshua (son of R' Akiva's father-in-law), Yadayim 3:5.
R’ Shimon ben Yehoshua, cited in Seder HaDorot from Yelammedenu, Beshalach.

notes.text: The consulted Mishnah has the same unpunctuated chain, Yochanan ben Yehoshua ben chamiv shel Rabbi Akiva. The parenthetical is preserved without deciding which generational attachment Hyman intended. Seder HaDorot is the ordinary expansion of סה״ד.

The earlier Yadayim3:5 comparison supplies the same compressed Yochanan-ben-Yehoshua/father-in-law chain. It does not determine the attachment of Hyman’s parenthesis; son-in-law is withdrawn as a translation, but neither generational attachment is canonized. The Bartenura nonmatch is an inherited bounded report, not a new commentary inspection. SederHaDorot is the contextual expansion of סה״ד beside olderOCRסה״ר, and YelammedenuBeshalach remains Hyman’s attribution. None of these exact occurrences has a new full-title witness; abbreviated R' is kept. Separate Yehoshua notices are not merged.

Hyman’s notice spans vol. II, pp. 619–620. Mishnah Yadayim 3:5 gives “Yochanan ben Yehoshua” followed by “son of Rabbi Akiva’s father-in-law.” The placement of Hyman’s parenthesis and the consulted commentaries leave its attachment open. Chullin 56b names Yose ben Yehoshua in a separate transmission. Seder HaDorot names Shimon ben Yehoshua and cites Yelammedenu, Beshalach.
